title: Evacuation Messages During the Wildfire
script: Sari: [urgent] Bram, the fire's jumped the ridge behind your street. Are you seeing this on the emergency alert yet?
Bram: [tense] Just got it. Honestly, the smoke's been thickening for an hour, but I assumed we still had time before it reached this side.
Sari: [firm] Assuming is exactly what gets people trapped. Please tell me you're packing the car right now, not debating it.
Bram: [reluctant] I'm grabbing documents and the dog, but part of me hates leaving before it's absolutely certain we'll need to.
Sari: [pressing] That hesitation is understandable, but by the time it's absolutely certain, the road out might already be blocked with traffic or worse.
Bram: [conceding] You're right, I know you're right. I just keep thinking about everything we can't fit in one car.
Sari: [gently] I get that completely, but none of it matters if you're not safely on the road within the next twenty minutes.
Bram: [determined] Okay. Photos, papers, the dog, and whatever medication we have. Everything else stays, and I'll try not to look back at the house.
Sari: [warmly] That's exactly the right call. Which route are you taking? The coastal road or the inland highway?
Bram: [thinking] Inland highway, probably, since the coastal road tends to bottleneck whenever there's an evacuation order for this whole district.
Sari: [agreeing] Good instinct. I'll text you updates from the news feed as they come in, so you're not checking your phone while driving.
Bram: [grateful] Thank you. I might have stayed another hour deliberating if you hadn't called.
Sari: [gently] That's what neighbors are for, even ones who moved away and now just watch the news anxiously from a distance.
Bram: [with feeling] I'm pulling out of the driveway now. The sky behind the house has gone this unsettling shade of orange.
Sari: [relieved] Just drive carefully and don't rush past the point of safety. The house is replaceable. You and the dog aren't.
Bram: [softly] I know. Still strange how quickly priorities sort themselves out once you're actually forced to choose.
Sari: [warmly] Call me the second you're clear of the district, whatever time it is. I won't be sleeping until I hear from you.
Bram: [sincerely] I will. Thank you for not letting me talk myself into staying any longer than I already did.

quiz.question: Why had Bram not left earlier?
options: He didn't receive any alert
He assumed they still had time before the fire reached his side
He was waiting for a friend
He didn't believe the fire was real
quiz.explanation: Bram assumed they still had time before the fire reached his side, even though smoke had been thickening for an hour.

quiz.question: What does Bram decide to take with him?
options: As much furniture as possible
Photos, papers, the dog, and medication
Only his phone and wallet
Nothing, he decides to stay
quiz.explanation: Bram decides to take photos, papers, the dog, and whatever medication they have, leaving everything else behind.

quiz.question: Which route does Bram choose and why?
options: The coastal road, because it's faster
The inland highway, since the coastal road tends to bottleneck during evacuation orders
He doesn't know which route to take
A route Sari has never heard of
quiz.explanation: Bram chooses the inland highway since the coastal road tends to bottleneck whenever there's an evacuation order.

quiz.question: What does Sari offer to do while Bram drives?
options: Nothing, she stays out of contact
Text him updates from the news feed so he's not checking his phone while driving
Drive to meet him halfway
Call the fire department for him
quiz.explanation: Sari offers to text him updates from the news feed as they come in, so he doesn't check his phone while driving.

quiz.question: What does Sari remind Bram at the end of the conversation?
options: That the house matters more than anything
That the house is replaceable, but he and the dog aren't
That he should have left the dog behind
That she is angry with him
quiz.explanation: Sari tells him to drive carefully and reminds him that the house is replaceable, but he and the dog aren't.
